content.content:
1	"""Durable JSON-file persistence for the device store.
2	
3	The whole server state is kept in one versioned JSON document. A missing file
4	is created on first use; a corrupted file or a document whose version is not
5	understood makes the server refuse to start (state is never silently
6	discarded). Every change is written atomically: serialize to a temporary file
7	in the same directory, ``fsync`` it, take a hard-link backup of the current
8	target, ``os.replace`` it over the target, then ``fsync`` the parent
9	directory, so a crash never leaves a half-written or un-renamed state file.
10	
11	Persistence is transactional with respect to the in-memory store: the change
12	hook fires while the store lock is held (the mutation is visible but not yet
13	committed to callers). When the durable write succeeds it becomes the new
14	last-known-good state. When writing the temporary file, ``fsync`` or the
15	atomic replace fails (an :class:`OSError`), the previous last-known-good state
16	is restored into memory under the same lock and
17	:class:`PersistenceUnavailable` is raised so the HTTP layer answers
18	503/field=data_file; the failed mutation therefore never advances either
19	memory or the file.
20	
21	After the replace has landed, a failed directory fsync first rolls the rename
22	back: the pinned old inode is renamed over the target and a second directory
23	fsync flushes the rollback. When that rollback itself cannot be completed
24	durably — the rollback rename fails, or the second fsync fails — the failure
25	stays *decidable*: the old inode is kept under a ``.state-*.bak`` backup and
26	the new snapshot is taken off the formal path (parked under a
27	``.state-*.quarantine`` name the recovery scan never promotes, or deleted), so
28	the formal path is missing. The store is then marked degraded and reports 503
29	for the failed request.
30	
31	The degraded store also heals itself *within the same process*: the next
32	persist-able write runs, inside the storage lock, :meth:`JsonStateStore.heal`
33	before saving — the unique pinned ``.bak`` is fully verified (version=1,
34	commit generation, the complete-transaction sections, every cross-entity /
35	cursor / nonce / audit-chain semantic check, and exact equality with the
36	last committed in-memory state) and atomically promoted back onto the formal
37	path, same-transaction leftovers (``.quarantine``/``.tmp``) are removed, and
38	only then is that one triggering request committed (a single consecutive
39	``commit_seq`` advance). The request that originally got 503 is never
40	replayed; the healed commit carries only the later, current request. A
41	corrupt, dangling or ambiguous backup is refused promotion: the request gets
42	503/field=data_file, memory is rolled back, the formal path stays missing,
43	no leftover or generation moves, and the next write retries the heal. A
44	valid formal file always takes precedence over every backup. Restart
45	recovery remains the fallback that promotes the pinned backup.
46	
47	A crash between steps can leave ``.state-*.tmp`` (staged document) or
48	``.state-*.bak`` (pinned previous inode) files beside the target. At the next
49	:func:`attach_persistence` these are resolved by
50	:func:`recover_crash_leftovers`: a valid formal file stays authoritative and
51	the leftovers are removed; with the formal file missing the highest
52	``commit_seq`` leftover that parses as version=1, carries the cursor and
53	``key_events`` sections (the footprint of one complete durable transaction),
54	and passes every semantic restore check is atomically recovered into place
55	(modification time newest-first breaks equal generations, and files without
56	the field keep the legacy newest-mtime rule); with none valid the leftovers
57	are removed and an empty state is created. An existing-but-corrupt formal
58	file still makes startup refuse rather than being silently overwritten.
59	
60	Every document carries a strictly-consecutive top-level ``commit_seq``: the
61	first empty state is written at 0 and each successful durable transaction
62	advances it exactly once (a failed write consumes no generation). A legacy
63	version=1 file without the field loads as generation 0; a present field must
64	be a non-negative integer or startup refuses (bool, negative, float and
65	string values are rejected) with the file untouched.
66	"""
67	from __future__ import annotations
68	
69	import copy
70	import errno
71	import json
72	import os
73	import sys
74	import tempfile
75	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
76	
77	from .storage import DeviceStore
78	
79	if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
80	    from .service import DeviceService
81	
82	#: Persistence format version understood by this build.
83	STATE_VERSION = 1
84	
85	#: Temporary-snapshot name parts, mirrored when scanning crash leftovers
86	#: (see :meth:`JsonStateStore.save`).
87	_TMP_PREFIX = ".state-"
88	_TMP_SUFFIX = ".tmp"
89	#: Suffix of the pre-replace hard-link backup pinning the previous inode.
90	_BAK_SUFFIX = ".bak"
91	#: Suffix of a new snapshot taken off the formal path when the rollback
92	#: itself cannot be completed durably. Such a file is deliberately *not* a
93	#: crash-recovery candidate (the scan only promotes ``.tmp``/``.bak``): the
94	#: transaction it staged was already reported failed and rolled back in
95	#: memory, so it must never be resurrected at the next startup.
96	_QUARANTINE_SUFFIX = ".quarantine"
97	
98	#: Top-level commit-generation field. Every successful durable transaction
99	#: writes a document whose ``commit_seq`` is exactly one higher than the
100	#: previous one; the first (empty) state is created at 0. A legacy version-1
101	#: file written before this field loads as if it carried 0.
102	COMMIT_SEQ_KEY = "commit_seq"
103	
104	
105	def _valid_commit_seq(value: Any) -> bool:
106	    """A commit generation is a non-negative JSON integer (never a bool)."""
107	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0
108	
109	
110	def _commit_seq_of(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> int:
111	    """Rank a candidate by its commit generation; a missing/malformed one is 0.
112	
113	    Leftover snapshots are ranked leniently here (a leftover without the field
114	    predates commit generations and sorts at generation 0); the *formal*
115	    file's field is validated strictly by :meth:`JsonStateStore.load`.
116	    """
117	    value = document.get(COMMIT_SEQ_KEY, 0)
118	    return value if _valid_commit_seq(value) else 0
119	
120	
121	class StateFileError(Exception):
122	    """The state file is missing fields, corrupt, or has an unknown version."""
123	
124	
125	class PersistenceUnavailable(Exception):
126	    """A durable write failed; the transaction was rolled back in memory.
127	
128	    The in-memory store was restored to the last successfully persisted state
129	    under the store lock, the previous state file is intact, and the temporary
130	    file was removed. The HTTP layer reports this as 503/field=data_file.
131	    """
132	
133	
134	class JsonStateStore:
135	    """Versioned JSON document loaded from and atomically saved to one file."""
136	
137	    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
138	        self.path = path
139	        #: Commit generation the *next* save writes. The first (empty) state
140	        #: is created at 0; :func:`attach_persistence` re-seeds it from a
141	        #: loaded or recovered document (plus one) so generations stay
142	        #: strictly consecutive across restarts and recovery. It advances
143	        #: only once a save has completed durably, so a failed transaction
144	        #: never consumes a generation.
145	        self.commit_seq = 0
146	        #: Set once a transaction ends in the undecidable-on-disk state where
147	        #: the formal path is missing and the last committed inode survives
148	        #: only as a ``.bak`` (a failed rollback rename, or a rollback rename
149	        #: whose follow-up fsync failed). While set, every write first runs
150	        #: :meth:`heal` under the store lock: the pinned backup is fully
151	        #: verified and atomically promoted back onto the formal path, the
152	        #: same-transaction leftovers are cleaned, and only then the
153	        #: triggering write itself is committed. A heal that cannot verify or
154	        #: promote the backup keeps the store degraded and the write fails
155	        #: with 503/field=data_file, retryable by the next write.
156	        self.degraded = False
157	
158	    def load(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
159	        """Load the document, or ``None`` when the file does not exist yet.
160	
161	        Raises :class:`StateFileError` if the file cannot be decoded as JSON,
162	        is not a JSON object, carries a missing/unknown ``version``, or has a
163	        ``commit_seq`` that is present but not a non-negative integer (a bool,
164	        negative number, float or string). A file without ``commit_seq`` is a
165	        legacy version-1 document and loads as generation 0.
166	        """
167	        try:
168	            with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
169	                raw = handle.read()
170	        except FileNotFoundError:
171	            return None
172	        except OSError as error:
173	            raise StateFileError(f"cannot read state file {self.path}: {error}")
174	
175	        try:
176	            document = json.loads(raw)
177	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
178	            raise StateFileError(
179	                f"state file is not valid JSON: {self.path} ({error})")
180	
181	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
182	            raise StateFileError("state document must be a JSON object")
183	        version = document.get("version")
184	        if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool):
185	            raise StateFileError("state document is missing a numeric 'version'")
186	        if version != STATE_VERSION:
187	            raise StateFileError(
188	                f"unsupported state file version: {version} "
189	                f"(this server supports {STATE_VERSION})")
190	        if COMMIT_SEQ_KEY in document:
191	            commit_seq = document[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY]
192	            if not _valid_commit_seq(commit_seq):
193	                raise StateFileError(
194	                    f"state document '{COMMIT_SEQ_KEY}' must be a "
195	                    f"non-negative integer")
196	        return document
197	
198	    def save(self, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
199	        """Atomically replace the file with *state* (version stamped).
200	
201	        Writes a sibling temporary file, fsyncs it, then ``os.replace`` and
202	        fsyncs the parent directory, so the rename itself is durable across
203	        a crash — the target is either the previous full document or the new
204	        full one, never a truncated mix.
205	
206	        Before the replace a hard link to the current target is taken in the
207	        same directory. If the replace itself succeeds but the following
208	        directory fsync fails, that link is renamed back over the target,
209	        restoring the previous document's exact bytes *and inode*, and the
210	        rollback is flushed with a second directory fsync; every other
211	        pre-replace failure simply removes the temporary file, leaving the
212	        target untouched.
213	
214	        When the rollback itself cannot be completed durably — the rollback
215	        rename fails, or the second directory fsync fails — the store falls
216	        back to a *decidable* crash state instead of risking an un-committed
217	        snapshot at the formal path: the last committed inode is kept under a
218	        ``.bak`` backup and the new snapshot is taken off the formal path
219	        (renamed aside to a ``.quarantine`` name the recovery scan never
220	        promotes, or deleted), so the formal path is missing and the next
221	        write self-heals via :meth:`heal` (or, after a restart,
222	        :func:`recover_crash_leftovers`). Any failure propagates the
223	        underlying :class:`OSError` to the caller.
224	        """
225	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))
226	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
227	        if self.degraded:
228	            # The formal path is missing and the last committed inode is
229	            # pinned only as a .bak. A save here could not be rolled back
230	            # (there is no target to back up), so the persistence hook must
231	            # run self.heal() first and only reach this point once the formal
232	            # path is restored. Refuse any save that bypassed the heal.
233	            raise OSError(
234	                f"state store for {self.path} is degraded; heal() must "
235	                f"promote the pinned backup before another save")
236	        document = {"version": STATE_VERSION, **state}
237	        # Stamp the commit generation this save is committing. The counter
238	        # advances only after the replace and directory fsync succeed, so a
239	        # failed transaction (rolled back below) consumes no generation and
240	        # the next retry rewrites the same one — generations on disk stay
241	        # strictly consecutive.
242	        seq = self.commit_seq
243	        document[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY] = seq
244	        tmp_handle = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
245	            mode="w", encoding="utf-8", dir=directory, delete=False,
246	            prefix=".state-", suffix=".tmp")
247	        tmp_path = tmp_handle.name
248	        backup_path: Optional[str] = None
249	        replaced = False
250	        try:
251	            json.dump(document, tmp_handle, separators=(",", ":"),
252	                      ensure_ascii=False)
253	            tmp_handle.flush()
254	            os.fsync(tmp_handle.fileno())
255	            tmp_handle.close()
256	            # Pin the old inode before renaming over it. On the first save the
257	            # target does not exist yet, so there is no old state to preserve.
258	            backup_path = _hardlink_backup(directory, self.path)
259	            os.replace(tmp_path, self.path)
260	            replaced = True
261	            # The rename is only durable once the directory entry is flushed;
262	            # without this fsync a crash can leave the directory pointing at
263	            # the pre-rename entry even though the replacement landed.
264	            _fsync_directory(directory)
265	        except BaseException:
266	            tmp_handle.close()
267	            _remove_quietly(tmp_path)
268	            if replaced and backup_path is not None:
269	                # The replacement landed but the following directory fsync
270	                # failed. Restore the pinned old inode atomically first (the
271	                # rename itself also drops the new inode)...
272	                try:
273	                    os.replace(backup_path, self.path)
274	                except OSError:
275	                    # ...the rollback rename itself failed. The formal path
276	                    # still holds the un-committed new inode, which must never
277	                    # become authoritative: move it off the path (the old
278	                    # inode stays pinned in the .bak), so the next startup
279	                    # sees a missing formal file and recovers that backup.
280	                    _vacate_new_snapshot(directory, self.path)
281	                    # Keep the backup: it is now the only copy of the last
282	                    # committed inode, so it must not be cleaned up below.
283	                    backup_path = None
284	                    self.degraded = True
285	                else:
286	                    backup_path = None
287	                    try:
288	                        _fsync_directory(directory)
289	                    except OSError:
290	                        # The rollback rename restored the old inode but its
291	                        # durability could not be flushed: this step failed
292	                        # too, so the transaction is still failed, never
293	                        # committed. Re-pin the restored inode as a .bak and
294	                        # vacate the formal path again, leaving exactly the
295	                        # "formal missing + old-inode .bak" state startup
296	                        # recovery resolves. When the path could not be
297	                        # vacated the old inode is still authoritative at it
298	                        # (the safe outcome), so the store is not degraded.
299	                        if _repin_old_inode(directory, self.path):
300	                            self.degraded = True
301	            if backup_path is not None:
302	                _remove_quietly(backup_path)
303	            raise
304	        # Commit is durable; drop the pinned old inode (best effort — a
305	        # leftover backup is harmless and cleaned up at the next startup).
306	        if backup_path is not None:
307	            _remove_quietly(backup_path)
308	            try:
309	                _fsync_directory(directory)
310	            except OSError:
311	                pass
312	        # The generation advances exactly once per durable commit.
313	        self.commit_seq = seq + 1
314	
315	    def heal(self, baseline: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
316	        """Self-heal the degraded formal path from the pinned ``.bak``.
317	
318	        Called under the store lock by the persistence hook at the start of
319	        the next persist-able write after an undecidable write failure. The
320	        pinned backup is verified in full — version=1, a valid commit
321	        generation exactly one below the next save's generation, the whole
322	        cross-entity/cursor/nonce/audit-chain semantic restore, and exact
323	        equality with the process's last committed in-memory state — before
324	        it is promoted. Promotion is a same-directory *hard link*: the backup
325	        name keeps pinning the inode until the formal directory entry is
326	        fsync-durable, so a crash at this instant leaves either a valid
327	        formal file or the still-present backup, never neither. Only then are
328	        the same-transaction leftovers (redundant backups, staged ``.tmp``
329	        snapshots and the un-committed ``.quarantine``) removed.
330	
331	        A later write commit still goes through the normal atomic
332	        :meth:`save`, so healing consumes no generation: the healed commit
333	        advances ``commit_seq`` exactly once and carries only that triggering
334	        request — the earlier request that got 503 is never replayed.
335	
336	        Raises :class:`OSError` (mapped to 503/field=data_file by the caller)
337	        when no verifiable backup exists, backups disagree, or the promotion
338	        cannot be made durable; in every such case the formal path stays
339	        missing, no leftover and no generation moves, :attr:`degraded` stays
340	        set, and the next write retries this heal. A formal file that
341	        reappeared valid and matching always takes precedence over backups.
342	        """
343	        if not self.degraded:
344	            return
345	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))
346	        leftovers = _leftover_tmp_paths(directory, self.path)
347	        quarantined = _quarantined_paths(directory, self.path)
348	
349	        if os.path.exists(self.path):
350	            # The formal path can only reappear out-of-band while degraded. A
351	            # valid one that matches the committed state always wins: keep it,
352	            # sweep every leftover and resume normal saves. Anything else is
353	            # left untouched — exactly the refusal a restart would give.
354	            formal = _read_version1_document(self.path)
355	            if (formal is not None
356	                    and (COMMIT_SEQ_KEY not in formal
357	                         or _valid_commit_seq(formal[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY]))
358	                    and _commit_seq_of(formal) == self.commit_seq - 1
359	                    and _document_restores(formal)
360	                    and _document_payload_equals(formal, baseline)):
361	                _sweep_leftovers(directory, leftovers + quarantined)
362	                self.degraded = False
363	                return
364	            raise OSError(
365	                f"cannot self-heal {self.path}: the formal file reappeared "
366	                f"in an unexpected state")
367	
368	        # Verify every leftover against this process's last committed state.
369	        # Equality with *baseline* is the anti-dangling gate in addition to
370	        # the full semantic restore: a staged new snapshot (the transaction
371	        # already reported 503 and rolled back in memory) parses and may even
372	        # restore, but it can never equal the committed baseline and is
373	        # therefore never eligible here; quarantine files are never even
374	        # considered.
375	        eligible: List[str] = []
376	        for candidate in leftovers:
377	            try:
378	                with open(candidate, "rb") as handle:
379	                    raw = handle.read()
380	            except OSError:
381	                continue
382	            try:
383	                document = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
384	            except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
385	                continue
386	            if not isinstance(document, dict):
387	                continue
388	            version = document.get("version")
389	            if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
390	                    or version != STATE_VERSION:
391	                continue
392	            if COMMIT_SEQ_KEY in document and not _valid_commit_seq(
393	                    document[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY]):
394	                continue
395	            # The backup must pin the immediately-previous generation (a
396	            # field-less legacy backup ranks at 0 with the counter at 1).
397	            if _commit_seq_of(document) != self.commit_seq - 1:
398	                continue
399	            if not _document_restores(document):
400	                continue
401	            if not _document_payload_equals(document, baseline):
402	                continue
403	            eligible.append(candidate)
404	
405	        if not eligible:
406	            raise OSError(
407	                f"cannot self-heal {self.path}: no verifiable pinned backup "
408	                f"of the last committed state")
409	        # Every eligible pin is the same generation and equals the committed
410	        # state, so choosing among them cannot diverge state; prefer a .bak
411	        # pin over a byte-identical staged .tmp, then the stable name order.
412	        eligible.sort(key=lambda path: (
413	            not path.endswith(_BAK_SUFFIX), path))
414	        chosen = eligible[0]
415	
416	        # Promote with a hard link, never a rename: the backup keeps pinning
417	        # the inode until the new formal directory entry is fsync-durable.
418	        linked = False
419	        try:
420	            os.link(chosen, self.path)
421	            linked = True
422	            _fsync_directory(directory)
423	        except OSError:
424	            if linked:
425	                # The entry may not be durable. Drop the name we just added —
426	                # the inode stays pinned under the backup name — and best
427	                # effort flush the removal, then hand the failure back.
428	                _remove_quietly(self.path)
429	                try:
430	                    _fsync_directory(directory)
431	                except OSError:
432	                    pass
433	            raise
434	
435	        # The formal path durably names the committed inode; every pinned
436	        # copy, staged snapshot and demoted (quarantined) new snapshot is now
437	        # stale garbage. Sweep failures are harmless: a valid formal file
438	        # always wins the leftover scan at every later startup.
439	        _sweep_leftovers(directory, leftovers + quarantined)
440	        self.degraded = False

443	def _directory_fsync_unsupported(error: OSError) -> bool:
444	    """Classify *error* as "this platform/filesystem cannot fsync a directory".
445	
446	    Some POSIX network or special filesystems reject ``fsync`` on a
447	    directory fd with ``EINVAL`` (others use ``ENOTSUP``/``EOPNOTSUPP``);
448	    on Windows a directory cannot be opened for this at all and the CRT
449	    fails with ``EACCES`` (older runtimes raise ``EISDIR``). None of these
450	    means the data write itself failed — the file fsync and the atomic
451	    rename already landed — so the directory flush is safely skipped
452	    instead of failing (and rolling back) the whole transaction. Genuine
453	    I/O errors (``EIO``, ``EBADF``, permission problems elsewhere, ...)
454	    still propagate.
455	    """
456	    unsupported = {errno.EINVAL, errno.ENOTSUP,
457	                   getattr(errno, "EOPNOTSUPP", None)}
458	    if error.errno in unsupported:
459	        return True
460	    if sys.platform == "win32" and error.errno in (errno.EACCES, errno.EISDIR):
461	        return True
462	    return False
463	
464	
465	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> bool:
466	    """Flush *directory*'s metadata so a recent rename survives a crash.
467	
468	    Returns ``True`` when the flush ran. When the platform or underlying
469	    filesystem cannot fsync directories, the capability is safely skipped
470	    (returns ``False``) without reporting a failure; every other
471	    :class:`OSError` propagates to the caller. On platforms without
472	    ``O_DIRECTORY`` the plain read-only open still works.
473	    """
474	    flags = os.O_RDONLY
475	    try:
476	        dir_fd = os.open(directory, flags)
477	    except OSError as error:
478	        if _directory_fsync_unsupported(error):
479	            return False
480	        raise
481	    try:
482	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
483	    except OSError as error:
484	        if _directory_fsync_unsupported(error):
485	            return False
486	        raise
487	    finally:
488	        os.close(dir_fd)
489	    return True

492	def _hardlink_backup(directory: str, target: str) -> Optional[str]:
493	    """Pin the current *target*'s inode via a same-directory hard link.
494	
495	    Returns the backup path, or ``None`` when *target* does not exist yet
496	    (first save: there is no old state to preserve). The link is created in
497	    the same directory so it is guaranteed to be on the same file system and
498	    the subsequent rollback ``os.replace`` is a pure metadata rename. Raises
499	    :class:`OSError` if the link cannot be made; the caller treats that like
500	    any pre-replace failure (the target is still untouched).
501	    """
502	    if not os.path.exists(target):
503	        return None
504	    fd, backup = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=_TMP_PREFIX,
505	                                  suffix=_BAK_SUFFIX)
506	    os.close(fd)
507	    try:
508	        # mkstemp created an empty file under that unique name; remove it so
509	        # the name is free for the hard link.
510	        os.unlink(backup)
511	        os.link(target, backup)
512	    except OSError:
513	        _remove_quietly(backup)
514	        raise
515	    return backup
516	
517	
518	def _quarantine_path(directory: str) -> str:
519	    """Reserve a unique same-directory name for a demoted new snapshot."""
520	    fd, quarantine = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=_TMP_PREFIX,
521	                                      suffix=_QUARANTINE_SUFFIX)
522	    os.close(fd)
523	    # The empty placeholder only reserves the unique name; free it for the
524	    # rename that moves the new snapshot aside.
525	    os.unlink(quarantine)
526	    return quarantine

529	def _vacate_new_snapshot(directory: str, target: str) -> None:
530	    """Take the un-committed new snapshot off the formal path.
531	
532	    Used when a post-replace failure cannot be rolled back durably: the new
533	    inode must never become authoritative, so it is renamed aside to a
534	    ``.quarantine`` name (which the crash-leftover scan never promotes), and
535	    if even that rename is impossible it is deleted. Either way the formal
536	    path is missing afterwards; a pinned ``.bak`` of the last committed
537	    inode is the recovery candidate the next startup promotes. Best effort
538	    only — a failure here is swallowed because the caller still reports the
539	    transaction as failed and the old inode stays pinned elsewhere.
540	    """
541	    try:
542	        quarantine = _quarantine_path(directory)
543	        try:
544	            os.replace(target, quarantine)
545	        except OSError:
546	            _remove_quietly(quarantine)
547	            raise
548	    except OSError:
549	        _remove_quietly(target)
550

552	def _repin_old_inode(directory: str, target: str) -> bool:
553	    """Re-pin the restored old inode as a ``.bak`` and vacate *target*.
554	
555	    The rollback rename restored the last committed inode at *target*, but
556	    flushing that rollback failed, so it cannot be treated as durable. Pin
557	    the inode under a fresh backup name, then drop *target* (a second hard
558	    link to the same inode, so the unlink loses nothing), recreating the
559	    same "formal missing + old-inode .bak" triage a plain rollback failure
560	    leaves. Returns ``True`` when the formal path was vacated. If the inode
561	    cannot be pinned a second time it simply stays on the formal path — the
562	    last good state — and the function returns ``False`` so the caller does
563	    not mark the store degraded while a good file is authoritative.
564	    """
565	    try:
566	        fd, backup = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=_TMP_PREFIX,
567	                                      suffix=_BAK_SUFFIX)
568	        os.close(fd)
569	        os.unlink(backup)
570	        os.link(target, backup)
571	    except OSError:
572	        _remove_quietly(backup)
573	        # A second hard link cannot be made; instead rename the restored
574	        # target itself to the backup name — one atomic rename both keeps
575	        # the old inode (under the .bak) and vacates the formal path.
576	        try:
577	            fd, backup = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=_TMP_PREFIX,
578	                                          suffix=_BAK_SUFFIX)
579	            os.close(fd)
580	            os.unlink(backup)
581	            os.replace(target, backup)
582	        except OSError:
583	            _remove_quietly(backup)
584	            return False
585	    else:
586	        # target and backup now name the same restored inode; dropping
587	        # target leaves the inode pinned exactly once, under the backup name.
588	        _remove_quietly(target)
589	    return not os.path.exists(target)

592	def _read_version1_document(path: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
593	    """Parse *path* as a version-1 state document, or ``None`` if absent.
594	
595	    Mirrors :meth:`JsonStateStore.load` for arbitrary candidate paths (crash
596	    leftovers rather than the formal file): JSON object carrying
597	    ``version == 1`` or missing/unknown, returns the raw document or ``None``
598	    for a missing/unreadable/undecodable/wrong-version candidate.
599	    """
600	    try:
601	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
602	            raw = handle.read()
603	    except OSError:
604	        return None
605	    try:
606	        document = json.loads(raw)
607	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
608	        return None
609	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
610	        return None
611	    version = document.get("version")
612	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
613	            or version != STATE_VERSION:
614	        return None
615	    return document

618	def _candidate_is_section_complete(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
619	    """Require the durable-transaction sections a real snapshot always has.
620	
621	    Every snapshot produced by :meth:`JsonStateStore.save` is one full
622	    transaction and therefore carries the per-device sync cursor sections
623	    (``group_sync_cursors`` and ``message_sync_cursors``) and the
624	    ``key_events`` audit-chain section, each as a list — an empty list when
625	    the section has no records, but never absent. A leftover that parses and
626	    restores yet omits one of these sections is a partial/legacy document,
627	    not a crashed atomic commit: recovering it could silently drop a device's
628	    resume cursor or its audit chain, so it is not a valid crash-recovery
629	    candidate (a section-less *formal* file is still loaded leniently on the
630	    normal path; this gate applies only to leftover-snapshot recovery).
631	    """
632	    return all(isinstance(document.get(name), list)
633	               for name in ("group_sync_cursors", "message_sync_cursors",
634	                            "key_events"))

637	def _document_restores(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
638	    """Full semantic verification against :meth:`DeviceStore.restore_state`.
639	
640	    A structurally valid version-1 document is only a recovery candidate when
641	    a fresh store accepts its payload — the same group-session references,
642	    sequence continuity, nonce-set, per-device cursor range and ``updated_at``
643	    checks applied to the formal file.
644	    """
645	    try:
646	        DeviceStore().restore_state(
647	            {key: value for key, value in document.items()
648	             if key != "version"})
649	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
650	        return False
651	    return True

654	def _document_payload_equals(document: Dict[str, Any],
655	                             baseline: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
656	    """Compare a document's payload with the process's last committed state.
657	
658	    The on-disk document wraps the store snapshot with ``version`` and
659	    ``commit_seq``; strip those envelope fields and compare the remainder,
660	    semantically, to *baseline* (a value straight from
661	    :meth:`DeviceStore.snapshot_state`). Comparison goes through a fresh
662	    :meth:`DeviceStore.restore_state` + :meth:`DeviceStore.snapshot_state`
663	    round-trip rather than a raw dict diff, so an older *committed* document
664	    that legitimately predates an optional section (``used_nonces``, the
665	    sync-cursor sections, ``key_events`` ...) still matches a baseline whose
666	    snapshot fills those with their defaults — while a newer, un-committed
667	    snapshot cannot, because its extra business state (a revoked device, an
668	    appended message) round-trips to a different snapshot. This is the
669	    anti-dangling gate for self-heal: verifiable but newer content is never
670	    promoted. Returns ``False`` for any document that does not restore.
671	    """
672	    payload = {key: value for key, value in document.items()
673	               if key not in ("version", COMMIT_SEQ_KEY)}
674	    try:
675	        candidate_store = DeviceStore()
676	        candidate_store.restore_state(payload)
677	        restored = candidate_store.snapshot_state()
678	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
679	        return False
680	    return restored == baseline

683	def _sweep_leftovers(directory: str, paths: List[str]) -> None:
684	    """Best-effort remove crash/transaction leftovers and flush the directory.
685	
686	    Used once a valid formal file is (re-)established authoritatively — by
687	    self-heal or restart recovery — after which pinned backups, staged
688	    ``.tmp`` snapshots and demoted ``.quarantine`` files are pure garbage.
689	    Removal failures are swallowed: a valid formal file wins the leftover
690	    scan at the next startup anyway, so a stray file can never become
691	    authoritative.
692	    """
693	    for path in paths:
694	        _remove_quietly(path)
695	    try:
696	        _fsync_directory(directory)
697	    except OSError:
698	        pass

701	def _leftover_tmp_paths(directory: str, target_path: str) -> List[str]:
702	    """List crash-leftover snapshots in *directory*.
703	
704	    These carry the same ``.state-`` prefix :meth:`JsonStateStore.save` uses,
705	    with either the ``.tmp`` suffix of a staged new document or the ``.bak``
706	    suffix of a pre-replace hard-link backup (the previous committed inode).
707	    The formal target itself is never considered.
708	    """
709	    try:
710	        names = os.listdir(directory)
711	    except OSError:
712	        return []
713	    leftovers: List[str] = []
714	    for name in names:
715	        if not name.startswith(_TMP_PREFIX):
716	            continue
717	        if not (name.endswith(_TMP_SUFFIX) or name.endswith(_BAK_SUFFIX)):
718	            continue
719	        full = os.path.join(directory, name)
720	        if os.path.abspath(full) == os.path.abspath(target_path):
721	            continue
722	        leftovers.append(full)
723	    return leftovers

726	def _quarantined_paths(directory: str, target_path: str) -> List[str]:
727	    """List demoted new snapshots parked under a ``.quarantine`` name.
728	
729	    These are never recovery candidates: a quarantined snapshot staged a
730	    transaction that was reported failed and rolled back in memory, so it is
731	    only garbage to remove once a valid formal state is authoritative (or a
732	    candidate has been recovered). A corrupt formal file keeps them on disk
733	    for inspection, like every other leftover.
734	    """
735	    try:
736	        names = os.listdir(directory)
737	    except OSError:
738	        return []
739	    quarantined: List[str] = []
740	    for name in names:
741	        if name.startswith(_TMP_PREFIX) and name.endswith(_QUARANTINE_SUFFIX):
742	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
743	            if os.path.abspath(full) != os.path.abspath(target_path):
744	                quarantined.append(full)
745	    return quarantined

748	def _remove_quietly(path: str) -> None:

755	def recover_crash_leftovers(state_store: "JsonStateStore") -> None:
756	    """Resolve temporary snapshots a crashed process left beside the file.
757	
758	    * A valid formal file wins outright: it is never overwritten, and every
759	      leftover is removed.
760	    * An existing but corrupt/invalid formal file is left untouched: the
761	      normal load then refuses startup, so present state is never silently
762	      discarded (and its leftovers are kept for inspection).
763	    * With the formal file missing, only candidates that parse as
764	      version=1, explicitly carry the
765	      ``group_sync_cursors``/``message_sync_cursors``/``key_events``
766	      sections (each a list — the footprint of one complete durable
767	      transaction), *and* pass full semantic verification are considered.
768	      They rank by commit generation first — the highest ``commit_seq``
769	      wins, so an older-mtime snapshot from a later generation is never
770	      lost to a newer-mtime stale one — with modification time newest-first
771	      among equal generations (a missing field counts as generation 0).
772	      When every candidate predates commit generations (none carries the
773	      field), selection stays the legacy newest-mtime rule. The chosen
774	      snapshot is atomically ``os.replace``-d into place (plus a
775	      parent-directory fsync) and the remaining leftovers are removed. A
776	      section-less legacy/partial snapshot is never promoted, so a resume
777	      cursor or the audit chain cannot be silently lost.
778	    * When no candidate is valid, all leftovers are removed; the normal
779	      missing-file path in :func:`attach_persistence` then creates an empty
780	      state.
781	    """
782	    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(state_store.path))
783	    leftovers = _leftover_tmp_paths(directory, state_store.path)
784	    quarantined = _quarantined_paths(directory, state_store.path)
785	    if not leftovers and not quarantined:
786	        return
787	
788	    if os.path.exists(state_store.path):
789	        # The formal file exists. A valid one stays authoritative and the
790	        # leftovers (including demoted snapshots parked in quarantine) are
791	        # stale; an invalid one (including a present but malformed
792	        # commit_seq) makes the normal load refuse startup, so neither the
793	        # file nor the leftovers are touched here.
794	        formal = _read_version1_document(state_store.path)
795	        formal_valid = (
796	            formal is not None
797	            and (COMMIT_SEQ_KEY not in formal
798	                 or _valid_commit_seq(formal[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY]))
799	            and _document_restores(formal))
800	        if formal_valid:
801	            for path in leftovers + quarantined:
802	                _remove_quietly(path)
803	        return
804	
805	    # Formal file missing. Verify every leftover first (unverifiable ones are
806	    # skipped), then rank the survivors by commit generation, not mtime: the
807	    # highest commit_seq wins even when a stale older-generation snapshot has
808	    # a newer mtime, and equal generations order newest-mtime-first. A
809	    # leftover without the field is a pre-generation snapshot at seq 0; when
810	    # every candidate is such a snapshot the ranking collapses to the legacy
811	    # pure-mtime rule. Ties in mtime break by name, deterministically.
812	    verified: List[Tuple[str, int, int]] = []
813	    any_with_seq = False
814	    for candidate in leftovers:
815	        document = _read_version1_document(candidate)
816	        if document is None or not _candidate_is_section_complete(document):
817	            continue
818	        # A present-but-malformed generation (bool, negative, float, string)
819	        # can never come from this build's atomic writer; promoting it would
820	        # only fail the strict formal-file load afterwards, so it is not a
821	        # verifiable candidate. A missing field is the legacy case and ranks
822	        # at generation 0.
823	        if COMMIT_SEQ_KEY in document and not _valid_commit_seq(
824	                document[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY]):
825	            continue
826	        if COMMIT_SEQ_KEY in document:
827	            any_with_seq = True
828	        if not _document_restores(document):

832	        except OSError:

835	
836	    recovered = None
837	    if verified:
838	        if any_with_seq:
839	            # Generation-first ordering; missing field ranks at 0, so a
840	            # present-generation snapshot always beats a field-less legacy
841	            # one regardless of mtime.
842	            verified.sort(key=lambda item: (item[1], item[2], item[0]))
843	        else:
844	            # Every candidate predates commit generations: keep the legacy
845	            # newest-mtime rule.
846	            verified.sort(key=lambda item: (item[2], item[0]))
847	        recovered = verified[-1][0]
848	
849	    if recovered is not None:
850	        os.replace(recovered, state_store.path)
851	        _fsync_directory(directory)
852	        leftovers = [path for path in leftovers if path != recovered]
853	    for path in leftovers:
854	        _remove_quietly(path)
855	    # A demoted snapshot is never a recovery candidate (its transaction was
856	    # reported failed and rolled back); once the formal path has been
857	    # resolved above, any quarantine file is pure garbage.
858	    for path in quarantined:
859	        _remove_quietly(path)
860

862	def attach_persistence(service: "DeviceService", path: str) -> JsonStateStore:
863	    """Load *path* into *service* and persist every subsequent change.
864	
865	    A missing file is created immediately (with an empty version-1 document).
866	    A corrupt or wrong-version file raises :class:`StateFileError` before the
867	    server starts; the in-memory store is never touched in that case. After
868	    attachment, each committed mutation rewrites the file atomically inside
869	    the same store-lock transaction. A write/fsync/replace failure rolls the
870	    in-memory store back to the last persisted state and raises
871	    :class:`PersistenceUnavailable`; neither memory nor the file advances.
872	    """
873	    state_store = JsonStateStore(path)
874	    # First resolve any temporary snapshot a crashed previous process left in
875	    # the same directory: a valid formal file stays and leftovers are removed;
876	    # a missing formal file is atomically restored from the newest verifiable
877	    # version-1 leftover; with no valid candidate the leftovers are removed and
878	    # the missing-file branch below creates an empty state.
879	    try:
880	        recover_crash_leftovers(state_store)
881	    except OSError as error:
882	        raise StateFileError(
883	            f"cannot recover state file {path} from a crash leftover: "
884	            f"{error}") from None
885	    document = state_store.load()
886	    if document is None:
887	        try:
888	            state_store.save(service.store.snapshot_state())
889	        except OSError as error:
890	            raise StateFileError(
891	                f"cannot create state file {path}: {error}") from None
892	    else:
893	        # Resume commit generations exactly where the durable document left
894	        # off (a legacy file without the field is generation 0): the next
895	        # successful transaction writes commit_seq + 1, never repeating or
896	        # skipping a generation after restart or crash recovery.
897	        state_store.commit_seq = _commit_seq_of(document) + 1
898	        try:
899	            service.store.restore_state(
900	                {key: value for key, value in document.items()
901	                 if key != "version"})
902	        except (ValueError, TypeError) as error:
903	            raise StateFileError(
904	                f"state file has a malformed payload: {error}") from None
905	
906	    # Canonical deep copy of the last durably-committed state. It is only ever
907	    # replaced with a snapshot whose save() succeeded, so it stays valid input
908	    # for restore_state().
909	    last_good: Dict[str, Any] = copy.deepcopy(service.store.snapshot_state())
910

912	        # Called under the store lock at the end of a mutation. Snapshot the
913	        # post-mutation state and try to durably commit it; on an I/O failure
914	        # roll the in-memory store back to the last good state before
915	        # surfacing the error, so the failed mutation is visible nowhere.
916	        pending = service.store.snapshot_state()
917	        if state_store.degraded:
918	            # A previous transaction ended undecidable on disk: the formal
919	            # path is missing and the last committed inode survives only as
920	            # a pinned .bak. Before this (the next) write may commit, verify

922	            # lock, cleaning the failed transaction's leftovers. Memory was
923	            # rolled back to last_good after the 503 and, like every later
924	            # failed attempt, restored to it again, so the only difference
925	            # between pending and last_good is *this* current request — the
926	            # earlier 503 request is never replayed.
927	            try:
928	                state_store.heal(copy.deepcopy(last_good))
929	            except OSError:
930	                service.store.restore_state(copy.deepcopy(last_good))
931	                raise PersistenceUnavailable(
932	                    f"could not self-heal state file {state_store.path}") \
933	                    from None
934	        try:
935	            state_store.save(pending)
936	        except OSError:
937	            service.store.restore_state(copy.deepcopy(last_good))
938	            raise PersistenceUnavailable(
939	                f"could not persist state to {state_store.path}") from None
